messages:
Maya Chen: Quick sprint check — noticed a P95 tail spike on the KV path after the kernel warmup change rolled out this morning. Can we confirm owners and next steps? Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/c/kv-warmup-canary

Jonah Patel: I can take the kernel side. My quick read: the new warmup handshake slightly increased concurrent KV reads under certain request shapes, hitting our shard lock contention. I have a draft fix (reduces unnecessary lock while populating the prefetch buffer). PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1289

Li Wei: Re: owners — prefetch team depends on the handshake semantics. If kernel reverts, prefetch should tolerate missing prefix entries. I added a small compatibility shim in prefetch that returns a soft-miss instead of throwing. PR: https://github.com/redwood/prefetch/pull/61

Serena Gomez: Timeline ask from product: can we do a hotfix tomorrow EOD? If it's safe to revert and ship, fine. If not, we need a canary plan and rollback window. Also need updated release notes and SLA impact statement.

Jonah Patel: Plan proposal: 1) push kernel patch (PR above) to canary at 11:30am, 2) 30min metric observation, 3) promote to 10% traffic if stable, 4) promote further after 2 hours. If regressions persist, revert via the rollback job. I can run the canary.

Maya Chen: Sounds good. @perf-bot can you start the canary once Jonah merges and post the job id? Also add latency alerts for p50/p95/p99 and KV error rate.

perf-bot: Canary job queued by Jonah Patel. job_id=canary-20260317-01. Metrics watching: runtime.latency.p50, runtime.latency.p95, runtime.kv.errors. Will post updates every 5m.

Li Wei: Minor note — prefetch PR includes a graceful fallback `kv.get_optional()` with the following change:

```diff
- val = kv.get(prefix)
- if not val:
-   raise PrefetchError
+ val = kv.get_optional(prefix)
+ if val is None:
+   # treat as cache miss and continue without failing
+   val = []
```

Jonah Patel: Merged kernel patch to canary branch and triggered canary. Link: https://ci.redwood/run/canary-20260317-01. Initial metrics look okay but there's a slight p95 blip at minute 7. Investigating lock hold times and sampling flame graphs now.

Maya Chen: If lock hold time is the culprit, can we reduce critical section quickly? If not, revert to previous kernel and then ship compatibility shim from prefetch. Which is lower risk?

Jonah Patel: Reducing critical section is my patch's intent — it should land within the next hour. If I can't get it stable by +90m, we'll revert. I'll post status here every 30m.

Serena Gomez: I'll prepare release note draft and SLA impact statement in case we need to notify customers. Tag me if you want me to open the incident or status page.

Maya Chen: Thanks. Quick ownership recap: kernel fix owner = Jonah Patel, prefetch compatibility = Li Wei, release/comms = Serena Gomez. I'll follow up in the sprint board and mark the "hotfix" lane.

Jonah Patel: Update +30m: flame graph shows a hot path in shard mutex during cold prefix population. The patch reduces mutex scope and defers non-critical work to a background task. Re-running canary.

perf-bot: Canary update for canary-20260317-01: p50=12ms, p95=210ms (improved from 280ms), kv.errors=0.002%. Next check in 25m.

Li Wei: Prefetch PR is ready for merge once kernel is promoted; it contains safe fallback for older kernels and an opt-in to use the new handshake. No breaking changes.

Maya Chen: Great — thanks all. If anything changes or you need pairing, ping me.

Jonah Patel: If we hit a regression after promotion I'll open an immediate rollback and call for on-call. For now continuing monitoring.

perf-bot: Last update (canary-20260317-01): p50=11ms, p95=198ms, p99=610ms, kv.errors=0.0018%. Canary stable at 10% for 45m.
